title: Backend API Auth, Token Expiry & Tenant IDOR Fixes

findings_remediated.SLAAT-P2-2-F1 (HIGH, fail-open bug, not: routers/discovery.py's GET /api/v1/discovery/workloads (and its /v1/ and bare mounts) forwarded to api_compat.list_discovery_workloads(request=request, principal=principal, status=..., source=..., namespace=..., search=...) -- kwargs that function has never accepted (its real signature is tenant_id: Depends(authenticated_tenant), source, status, namespace, search, page, limit). Every authenticated call raised TypeError inside route dispatch, turned into an unhandled 500 by FastAPI's exception middleware. A route that always 500s fails OPEN on an exception, not closed, and never actually reached the tenant-filtered DB query it was meant to expose. Fixed by deriving tenant_id from the already-authenticated principal and calling the real signature. Also closed five latent test failures in test_agent_discovery.py and test_connectors.py that were hitting the same crash.
findings_remediated.SLAAT-P2-2-F2 (HIGH, unauthenticated end: routers/compliance.py's POST /api/v1/compliance/posture/calculate had no Depends() at all -- any anonymous caller could reach it. Fixed by adding tenant_id: str = Depends(authenticated_tenant); the handler performs pure arithmetic over the request body and reads no tenant-owned data, so the dependency is an auth gate only.
findings_remediated.SLAAT-P2-2-F3 (HIGH, unauthenticated end: routers/policies.py's POST /api/v1/policies/validate had no Depends() at all -- any anonymous caller could reach the CEL syntax validator. Fixed the same way as F2. Note: the existing generic test_unauthenticated_mutation_fails_closed sweep in test_adversarial_api_security.py already targets routers.policies but could not have caught this -- it accepts 422 as a passing status, and this handler also returns 422 for malformed input regardless of authentication, so the missing auth dependency was masked by a coincidentally-identical status code for the empty-body probe payload the sweep sends. test_api_auth_remediation.py closes that blind spot with a well-formed, otherwise-200 payload.
findings_remediated.SLAAT-P2-2-F4 (test-harness defect, not: tests/test_tenant_isolation.py's EAP route sweep (_eap_http_routes, and the structural mount-dependency check in test_every_eap_route_carries_the_mount_level_auth_dependency) walked app.routes expecting flat APIRoute entries. This FastAPI version (0.140.7, newer than the apparently-pinned 0.115.6) wraps every include_router() mount in an opaque _IncludedRouter, so the flat isinstance() check silently saw zero EAP routes -- EAP_TENANT_BOUND_ROUTES came back empty, which cascaded into 3 more test failures (the mount-dependency check, the exemption-list guard, and the declared-attack-case collection count). Direct introspection confirmed the actual mount-level dependencies=[Depends(api_compat.authenticated_principal)] protection on all five EAP routers was intact throughout -- this was a test-tooling regression caused by a FastAPI version drift, not a live security gap. Fixed by adding a recursive _iter_app_routes / _iter_app_routes_with_mount_deps helper (mirroring the already-correct pattern in test_tenant_authorization_matrix.py) that descends through _IncludedRouter.original_router.routes and reads dependencies from _IncludedRouter.include_context.dependencies, which is where this FastAPI version actually stores router-level dependencies (verified by reading fastapi.routing source directly).

route_sweep_classification.before: 51 of app's registered /api* routes were in neither DB_ROUTES, NOT_DATABASE_BACKED, nor EAP_TENANT_BOUND_ROUTES -- i.e. nothing checked their tenant scoping. 32 of the 51 were EAP routes hidden by the SLAAT-P2-2-F4 test bug above; fixing F4 alone closed those.
route_sweep_classification.after: 0 unclassified, 0 stale entries. Remaining 18 non-EAP routes individually audited and classified: 3 added to DB_ROUTES (GET /api/v1/agents, POST /api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/transition, POST /api/v1/discovery/claim -- all independently verified tenant-scoped, now covered by the cross-tenant parametrised sweep test_every_database_statement_is_bound_to_the_callers_tenant), 15 added to NOT_DATABASE_BACKED with a documented reason each (cAdvisor telemetry, static compliance catalog, policy-engine proxy routes with server-derived tenant_id, and the two newly-authenticated pure-computation endpoints from F2/F3).

residual_findings_not_fixed_in_scope.cadvisor-telemetry-cross-tenant-read (ME: GET /api/telemetry/agents{,/{pod_name}} and their /api/v1/ duplicates (cadvisor_poller.py) are authenticated (router-level Depends(authenticated_principal)) but not tenant-partitioned: AgentTelemetry and the poller's pod index carry namespace/pod_name only, no tenant_id. An authenticated tenant that knows or guesses another tenant's pod_name can read its cAdvisor metrics. Not fixed: retrofitting a tenant-to-pod mapping onto cluster-wide cAdvisor scraping is a product decision about where that mapping lives (there is no tenant_id anywhere in this subsystem to filter by), the same shape as the pre-existing, already-escalated RBAC finding below. Classified NOT_DATABASE_BACKED with the gap documented in the sweep table rather than silently excused.
residual_findings_not_fixed_in_scope.rbac-cluster-id-no-tenant-mapping (pre-e: POST /api/rbac/clusters/{cluster_id}/{jobs,scan} share the same root cause as the already-pinned test_rbac_correlation_routes_are_not_tenant_scoped_at_all: authenticated via Depends(authenticated_tenant), but the upstream KubeSec-AFM call is built straight from the path's cluster_id with no tenant-to-cluster mapping anywhere in the service. Extended the existing, already-escalated finding to cover these two routes rather than re-litigating it.

verification.pytest_test_tenant_isolation: 153/153 pass (up from 148 passed / 5 failed before this card)
verification.pytest_fe_signalloom_full_suite_offline: 2416 passed, 103 skipped, 1 xfailed, 55 failed -- all 55 failures confirmed pre-existing via a stash-isolated baseline diff (comm -13/-23 on sorted FAILED lists before/after this card's changes): zero new regressions, 11 tests newly passing (the 5 test_tenant_isolation.py fixes above, plus 5 in test_agent_discovery.py and 1 in test_connectors.py that were hitting the same discovery.py TypeError crash from a different angle). The 4 respx-ImportError collection errors (test_agent_compliance.py, test_federation.py, test_latent_defects.py, test_policy_engine.py) are a missing-dependency environment gap unrelated to this card and were excluded from both runs identically.
verification.unittest_fake_integration_proxy: 53/53 pass, unaffected by this card (different app, outside merge boundary)
verification.manual_repro_discovery_workloads_crash: GET /api/v1/discovery/workloads with a valid bearer token returned 500 (TypeError: list_discovery_workloads() got an unexpected keyword argument 'request') before the fix; returns 200 with a well-formed DiscoveryWorkloadsResponseModel body after

not_applicable_to_this_repo.jwt_algorithm_whitelist_none_rejection_c: Already implemented and tested pre-SLAAT (api_compat.validate_jwt enforces RS256-only decode allowlist, required iss/sub/aud/exp claims, kid verification against JWKS) -- see test_token_adversarial_verification.py (36/36, unaffected) and test_tenant_isolation.py's token-forgery section (test_alg_none_is_rejected_by_the_algorithm_check_not_by_a_parse_error, test_an_rs256_token_resigned_hs256_with_the_public_key_is_rejected, etc., all passing, unchanged by this card).
not_applicable_to_this_repo.token_revocation_blacklist_refresh_rotat: This service is a Dex-OIDC Bearer-token relying party, not a token issuer -- it has no session/refresh-token lifecycle of its own to rotate or revoke. scripts/test-token-revocation.py and a Redis-backed revocation blacklist named in the card's Required Tests/Approach do not correspond to anything in this repo; same class of literal-path/architecture mismatch already documented by SLAAT-P1-2's errata for test/test_api_auth_tamper.py and security/payloads.txt.
not_applicable_to_this_repo.rate_limiting_middleware: Confirmed absent pre-existing finding (SLAAT-P1-2 API-F1, MEDIUM), reproduced unchanged by test_no_rate_limiting_middleware_is_installed (still passing as a documented-absence assertion, not a regression). Implementing rate limiting middleware was not undertaken in this L-sized card given the volume of higher-severity auth-bypass and route-classification work found and fixed; recommended as the next SLAAT-P2-2-adjacent follow-up.
